statement: Let T be an invertible measure-preserving transformation of a standard Borel probability space (E,P), I its invariant sigma-field modulo P-null sets, and Q=fP with f>=0 and integral f dP=1. On an extension with independent uniforms, there is an almost surely finite integer N>=0 and Z~P such that T^N Z~Q if and only if E[f|I]=1 almost surely. N need not be a path-filtration stopping time or have finite mean.

statement: For n>=2 let q_n(i)=n/(2 H_{n-1} i(n-i)), 1<=i<n, where H_m=sum_{j=1}^m 1/j. Conditional on a split i,n-i assume independent daughter trees of their respective sizes. If S is external path length and C is the sum of the absolute differences of daughter leaf counts, then G_n(u,v)=E[u^S v^C] satisfies G_1=1 and G_n=sum_i q_n(i) u^n v^{abs(n-2i)} G_i G_{n-i}. This identifies each finite-n joint law; it does not identify a limiting law.

statement: In a finite-leaf Markov branching tree with split probabilities q_n(i) and independent daughter trees conditional on i, an additive index A with deterministic root toll t^A_n(i) has mean mu^A_n=sum_i q_n(i)(t^A_n(i)+mu^A_i+mu^A_{n-i}). Put d^A_n(i)=t^A_n(i)+mu^A_i+mu^A_{n-i}-mu^A_n. For two finite-second-moment additive indices A,B, their covariance K_n=sum_i q_n(i)(K_i+K_{n-i}+d^A_n(i)d^B_n(i)). Setting B=A gives the variance recursion. Initial one-leaf values are deterministic.

statement: For a>=2 and b>=0, set lambda=(a,a-1,1^b) and mu=(a-1,a-1,1^{b+1}). Their standard Young tableau dimensions satisfy dim(mu)/dim(lambda)=a(a+b-1)/(2(a+b)(b+1)). In particular, for a=b+4 and b>=2 the diagram lambda has width minus number of rows equal to two, yet moving its top-right box to a new bottom row strictly decreases dimension. The ratio tends to 1/2. This refutes that specific move rule, not maximal-dimension uniqueness.

statement: Let (B^k)_{k in Z} be mutually independent standard Brownian drivers, and let the entire sequence of positive finite lengths (L_k) be independent of every driver, with partial sums diverging in both directions. Concatenate B^k restricted to [0,L_k] and pin the join between -1 and 0 at time and value zero. The resulting process has two-sided Wiener law at that origin. The lengths may have any joint law; no iid, uniform bound or finite-mean assumption is needed. Path-dependent Brownian stopping lengths are not covered.

statement: Assume the ordered stationary drift-jump particle law has its consistent RSK rank representation: first-row labels B=(1=b_1<...<b_k) from uniform permutations restricted to their smallest M labels, and independent unit-rate Poisson arrival spacings, giving independent conditional gamma gaps of shapes b_i-b_{i-1}, with X_1 of shape one. Truncating the nonnegative mixture to b_k<=M omits exactly epsilon_{k,M}=(1/M!) sum_{lambda partition of M, lambda_1<k}(f^lambda)^2, where f^lambda is the number of standard Young tableaux of shape lambda. The density L1 error is epsilon_{k,M}; all event-probability errors and the total variation after normalization are at most epsilon_{k,M}, using sup-event total variation. For k=2 epsilon=1/M!.

statement: Under the stationary RSK rank mixture for drift dX_i/dt=X_i and rate-one Poisson space-time left jumps, the first-row label pair is (1,b) with weight (b-1)/b!, b>=2. For 0<x_1<x_2, put g=x_2-x_1. Its joint density is exp(-x_2) F(g), where F(g)=sum_{r>=0}(r+1)g^r/(r!(r+2)!). Consequently X_1~Exp(1) is independent of X_2-X_1, whose density is exp(-g)F(g); F(0)=1/2. The marginal tail is P(X_2>x)=exp(-x) sum_{r>=0}x^r/(r!)^2.

statement: For h>=0 put F(h)=floor(exp(h)(1+sin(h)/4)). This is a finite integer-valued nondecreasing right-continuous counting function, realized by nonnegative deterministic heights. For L(beta)=integral_0^infinity exp(-beta h)F(h) dh, beta>1, (beta-1)L(beta)->1 as beta decreases to one, while exp(-h)F(h) has subsequential limits 5/4 and 3/4. Thus a real-axis pole residue and monotonicity do not alone imply the pointwise exponential-growth limit. This array is not a DGFF cluster.

statement: Consider independent offspring in generation j with pgf f_{a_j}(s)=1-(1-s)/(1+a_j(1-s)), a_j in {1,2}. Each generation has mean one and variance 2a_j. Survival to generation n from one ancestor has probability p_n=1/(1+sum_{j=1}^n a_j). Alternating a_j=1 and 2 in blocks of lengths 10^(2^(k+1)), k>=0, yields order-1/n survival but n p_n has subsequential limits one and one-half. This refutes a generic inference from bounded critical branching comparisons to an exact constant, not a percolation conjecture.

statement: For arbitrary real coefficients a_0,...,a_m, the polynomial P(z)=sum_{j<=m}a_j z^j and the formal series P(z)+sum_{n>m}n! z^n have identical supplied coefficients, but radii of convergence infinity and zero respectively. Alternating factorial signs still give zero radius. A factorial upper bound alone is compatible with either alternative. This gives no divergence result for actual self-avoiding-walk coefficients.

statement: In nearest-neighbor Z^2, for L=8^j join squares [-L,L-1]^2 and [3L,5L-1] x [-L,L-1] by {(x,-L):L<=x<3L}. The induced sets are connected, nested and exhausting, have volume 8L^2+2L and edge boundary 20L-2, hence form a Folner exhaustion. Any internal path between their squares uses all 2L+1 corridor edges. In iid bond percolation with p<1, its probability is at most p^(2L+1). This does not disprove existence of a different good Folner sequence.

statement: For the two-square Folner exhaustion with side 2L and a width-one corridor of length 2L, assume under fixed iid bond percolation p<1 that each square restricted to the ambient infinite cluster has one component of size (theta+o_P(1))4L^2, theta>0, and all its other components are o_P(L^2). Then with probability tending to one the two giants are separate within the exhaustion. The second-largest/largest ratio tends to one in probability, and the largest density tends to theta/2. The conclusion is conditional on those finite-square giant assumptions.

statement: For a closed K subset of R^2, call a boundary point z accessible from a component U of R^2 minus K if a continuous path starts at z and lies in U at every positive parameter. Join two complement components in a graph when some point of K is accessible from both. Two distinct points outside K can be joined by an arc meeting K finitely many times exactly when their components are joined by a finite graph path. Thus the simultaneous all-pairs property is equivalent to connectivity of this countable graph. Closure contact alone is insufficient.

statement: Let K be the unit circle together with all circles of radii 1+1/n, n>=1. K is compact. Every continuous path from the origin to a point of radius three intersects each of those circles by the intermediate value theorem, so no such path has finitely many K-contacts. The inner disk is isolated in the accessible adjacency graph. This is a deterministic compact-set example, not Brownian-trace evidence.
